figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1 | Evolutionary relationships of Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus. Hierarchical orthologue clustering was used to infer the evolutionary history of 
contemporary genes along the species phylogeny. Branch labels denote the number of gene gains (green) and gene losses (red) assigned to this branch. 
a, Last common ancestor (LCA) of Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus (XPF). b, LCA of Photorhabdus. c, LCA of Xenorhabdus. The tree topology was inferred 
from a maximum likelihood tree reconstruction based on a super matrix of 632 core proteins present in all 76 species. Splits consistently resolved in 3/3 
non-overlapping partitions of the core gene set are drawn in black. Grey branches denote splits consistently resolved in 2/3 non-overlapping partitions. 
The dashed branch indicates a split that is seen only in one partition. The consensus of these trees, including branch support values, is provided in 
Supplementary Fig. 3.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2 | Phyletic distribution of biosynthetic gene clusters in the Xenorhabdus/Photorhabdus family (XPF) clade. Taxon sampling was limited to those 
Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus strains with high-quality genome sequences available. A lower triangle indicates the presence of a gene cluster in the 
respective genome evidenced by the detection of an orthologue to the published gene clusters. An upper triangle represents compounds that were 
identified after extraction of liquid cultures followed by high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. For metabolites whose gene clusters 
are not known (green squares), compounds were identified using the masses and associated spectra, as reported in previous work (see Supplementary 
Table 7 for an overview of known compounds, and their mass(es) and respective references). Symbols in the column annotation indicate merged natural 
product groups: *dialkylresorcinols/cyclohexanediones, †lumizinones/pyrazinones, ‡small depsipeptides (xenematides/xeneprotides/xenobactins/
fatflabets), §(pre)xeno-/amicoumacins, ∥tryptamide/nematophins.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3 | Network analysis of 30 Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus strains. 
Shown are 3,297 nodes connected in networks with at least one neighbour 
(except tilivalline). Subnetworks containing known natural products 
are highlighted: ambactins (1), anthraquinones (2), dialkylresorcinols/
cyclohexanedions (3), GameXPeptides/xenotetrapeptide (4), glidobactins 
(5), PAX peptides (8), photopyrones (9), phurealipids (10), pyrrolizidine 
alkaloids (11), rhabdopeptides (12), rhabduscins (13), tilivalline (14), 
xefoampeptides (15), xenematides/xeneprotides/xenobactins/fatflabets 
(16), xenoamicins (17), (pre-)xeno-/amicoumacins (18), xenocyloins 
(19), xenorhabdins (20), xenortides (21), lumizinones/pyrazinones (22), 
phenylethylamides (23), szentiamides (24), taxlllaids (25), tryptamide/
nematophins (26), xenofuranones (27), xentrivalpeptides (28). Further 
details of 1–28 are provided in Supplementary Table 7.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4 | GameXPeptide and xefoampeptide subnetworks and structures. a, Detailed 40-node subnetwork presenting molecularly characterized (large 
circles) and unidentified (small circles) nodes representing cyclic peptides that contain the known GameXPeptides (4a–f). Colours represent four- 
(yellow), five- (green) and six- (blue) membered rings. b, Structures of GameXPeptide (GXP) (4a–f) and related hexa- and tetrapeptides (4g–i) present in 
the network given in single amino-acid code with lower-case letters for d-amino acids. *Indicates structure prediction, not differentiating between isobaric 
Leu/Ile and unknown stereochemistry. c, The eight-node xefoampeptide (XFP) (15a–e) subnetwork. d, Non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) module 
organization of the responsible NRPSs and structures of the xefoampeptides, of which 15a was elucidated by 1D and 2D NMR and all other derivatives by 
MS/MS analysis as well as prediction from the BGC, as described in the Supplementary Results. C, ​condensation; A, adenylation; T, thiolation;  
E, epimerization; TE, thioesterase domains. All precursor ion masses are indicated in the nodes.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5 | Subnetwork of depsipeptides and known structures. a, Detailed view of the 68-node depsipeptide subnetwork. b–e, Nodes are coloured to 
correspond to the identified NPs and their given structures—xenematides (16a–c, green, b), fatflabets (16e–j, blue, c), xenobactin (16d, orange, d) and 
xeneprotide (16k, yellow, e)—and unidentified compounds (white circles), which are related to the known depsipeptides. Precursor ion masses are given in 
the nodes. For details of the structure elucidation, see Supplementary Results. 16c* are isobaric species.
